profile.reading: This is Exatel S.A.s Modulowe Data Center, or Modular Data Center, in Warsaw, Poland, though no public source found this session discloses a specific street address, power capacity in megawatts, floor area, or opening year for this particular building, an honest gap this registry records rather than estimates. Exatel itself was formed October 1, 2004 through the merger of Tel-Energo, a state controlled telecom operator that leased communication lines, and TelBank, a banking sector data transmission provider, a corporate integration that took roughly a year and a half, with the merged company controlling more than 15,000 kilometers of fiber running at 320 gigabits per second and, at founding, majority owned by Polskie Sieci Elektroenergetyczne, the Polish power grid operator. Exatel later became part of the PGE Polska Grupa Energetyczna energy groups capital structure before ownership transferred from PGE to the Polish State Treasury on March 29, 2017, following a sale process that began in June 2016, with the transfer signed on the states behalf by then Minister of National Defense Antoni Macierewicz; Exatels own leadership framed the change as part of building a National Strategic Network Operator and advancing what it called Polands cyber sovereignty. The company remains 100 percent State Treasury owned as of its own current public materials, and today operates within Polands critical infrastructure and cybersecurity space, including involvement in civil protection systems alongside Polands Ministry of Interior and Administration. Exatel also plays a role in Polands 5G rollout and network security landscape, marketing itself to government and critical infrastructure clients specifically because of its wholly state owned status, a positioning distinct from privately or foreign owned Polish telecom competitors also tracked elsewhere in this registry, such as Orange Polska and T-Mobile Polska.
